United States Commission on International Religious Freedom Reauthorization Act of 2026
This bill reauthorizes the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom through 2028. The commission is an independent federal commission tasked with monitoring international religious freedom conditions, reviewing U.S. government policy, and making policy recommendations. posts.title: Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026
posts.label: 📌 Presented to President
posts.summary:
Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026
This bill reauthorizes through FY2031 and revises programs that support research and development of drugs and other therapies to address amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (also known as ALS or Lou Gehrig's disease) and other neurodegenerative diseases.
The bill reauthorizes
grants from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) for scientific research on investigational drugs to prevent or treat ALS for individuals not otherwise eligible for clinical trials,
grants from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for research and development of therapies to prevent and treat ALS and other neurodegenerative diseases, and
a Public-Private Partnership including the FDA and NIH that supports development and regulatory review of treatments for neurodegenerative diseases.
Also, the NIH, in considering renewal of its grants, must assess available information on the safety and efficacy of the investigational drugs. It must also require grantees to promptly report serious and unexpected adverse events associated with their investigational drugs.
Additionally, the FDA must publish a plan describing actions it will take over a five-year period to foster development of safe and effective drugs, and facilitate access to investigational drugs, that treat ALS and other rare neurodegenerative diseases. The FDA must also publish a report describing the actions it has taken under the plan.
posts.summaryLabel: Congressional Research Service, Reported to House
posts.meta: Energy and Commerce Committee · Rep. Mike Quigley (D-IL)
posts.whatsNext: President has 10 days (Sundays excepted): sign, veto, or it becomes law unsigned (pocket veto if adjournment prevents return)

aiSummaries.text:
This bill extends several federal programs through fiscal year 2031 that fund research and development of drugs and other treatments for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS, also called Lou Gehrig's disease) and other brain-related diseases that get worse over time.

Three programs are renewed. The National Institutes of Health (NIH) can keep giving grants for research on experimental drugs to prevent or treat ALS for people who can't otherwise join clinical trials. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) can keep giving grants to develop therapies for ALS and other neurodegenerative diseases. A public-private partnership involving the FDA and NIH can also keep supporting the development and regulatory review of treatments for these diseases.

The bill adds some safety requirements. When the NIH decides whether to renew one of these grants, it must review the available information on how safe and effective the experimental drug is. It must also require grant recipients to report serious and unexpected side effects promptly.

The FDA must publish a five-year plan describing what it will do to encourage the development of safe and effective drugs for ALS and other rare neurodegenerative diseases, and to make experimental drugs easier to access. Afterward, it must publish a report on the actions it has taken under that plan.

posts.title: Reversionary Interest Conveyance Act
posts.label: 📜✍️ Signed by Pres. Trump
posts.summary:
Reversionary Interest Conveyance Act
This bill directs the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) to offer to sell the reversionary interest of the United States in approximately 8.43 acres of land in Sacramento, California, as generally depicted on a specified map dated November 7, 2022. Within two years of receiving a request from the owner of the land, the BLM must offer the reversionary interest and convey the reversionary interest to the buyer upon payment. The payment must be in an amount that is at least the fair market value of the reversionary interest. The buyer must also pay all costs related to the applicable conveyance of the reversionary interest, including all surveys, appraisals, and other administrative costs.
The bill subjects the conveyance to valid existing rights.
The proceeds from the sale must be deposited into Federal Land Disposal Account.

posts.meta: Energy and Natural Resources Committee, Natural Resources Committee · Rep. Doris Matsui (D-CA)

aiSummaries.text:
The Reversionary Interest Conveyance Act would require the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) to offer to sell the United States' reversionary interest in about 8.43 acres of land in Sacramento, California. The land is shown on a map dated November 7, 2022. A reversionary interest is the government's right to get the land back under certain conditions.

If the owner of the land asks, the BLM must make the offer within two years of receiving the request. Once the buyer pays, the BLM must transfer the reversionary interest to them. The price must be at least the fair market value of that interest. The buyer also has to cover all costs of the transfer, including surveys, appraisals, and other administrative expenses.

The sale is subject to valid existing rights, meaning any rights that already legally apply to the land still hold. The money from the sale must be deposited into the Federal Land Disposal Account.

posts.title: Southcentral Foundation Land Transfer Act of 2025
posts.label: 📜✍️ Signed by Pres. Trump
posts.summary:
Southcentral Foundation Land Transfer Act of 2025
This bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to convey approximately 3.4 acres in Anchorage, Alaska, to the Southcentral Foundation (SCF) for use in connection with health and social services programs.
The conveyance must be made by warranty deed. The conveyance may not (1) require any consideration (such as payment) from the SCF for the property; (2) impose any obligation, term, or condition on the SCF relating to that property; or (3) allow for any U.S. reversionary interest in the property.
HHS must be accorded any easement or access to the property as may be reasonably necessary to satisfy any retained obligation or liability of HHS.
The bill prohibits the SCF from being liable for certain environmental contamination that occurred on or before the date on which the property is conveyed to the SCF. In turn, HHS may not be liable for any contamination that occurred after the date that the SCF controlled, occupied, and used the property.
posts.summaryLabel: Congressional Research Service, Reported to House
posts.committee: Indian Affairs Committee, Energy and Commerce Committee, Natural Resources Committee
posts.meta: Indian Affairs Committee, Energy and Commerce Committee, Natural Resources Committee · Rep. Nicholas Begich (R-AK)
posts.whatsNext: Takes effect (on enactment unless the text sets other dates)

aiSummaries.text:
The Southcentral Foundation Land Transfer Act of 2025 would require the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to transfer about 3.4 acres of land in Anchorage, Alaska, to the Southcentral Foundation (SCF). The land would be used for the foundation's health and social service programs.

The land must be transferred through a warranty deed, which is a document that gives the buyer a guarantee of clear ownership. The transfer cannot require the SCF to pay anything for the property. It also cannot place any duty, term, or condition on the SCF about the land, and it cannot give the federal government a right to take the property back later.

HHS would keep whatever easement or access rights to the property it reasonably needs to meet any obligation or liability it still has.

The SCF would not be held responsible for environmental contamination that happened on or before the date the land is transferred to it. In the same way, HHS would not be responsible for contamination that happened after the SCF began controlling, occupying, and using the property.

posts.title: Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act
posts.label: 📜✍️ Signed by Pres. Trump
posts.summary:
Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act
This act requires the Department of Labor to provide training and education to its employees on how to effectively assist law enforcement in detecting human trafficking.
The act directs Labor to determine which employees should receive the training and education based on their official duties. Further, it requires the training and education to include information that is appropriate for the employees' location or environment; that reflects current trends and best practices for the location or environment; and that is relevant to detecting human trafficking, identifying suspected victims, and referring potential cases to the Department of Justice and other appropriate authorities.
posts.summaryLabel: Congressional Research Service, Public Law
posts.meta: Education and Workforce Committee · Rep. Tim Walberg (R-MI)
posts.whatsNext: Takes effect (on enactment unless the text sets other dates)

aiSummaries.text:
The Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act requires the Department of Labor to train and educate its employees on how to help law enforcement spot human trafficking.

The Department of Labor decides which employees need this training based on their job duties.

The training must fit the setting where employees work, reflect current trends and good practices for that setting, and cover how to detect human trafficking, recognize people who may be victims, and pass possible cases on to the Department of Justice and other appropriate authorities.

posts.title: Vicksburg National Military Park Boundary Modification Act
posts.label: 📜✍️ Signed by Pres. Trump
posts.summary:
Vicksburg National Military Park Boundary Modification Act
This bill directs the Department of the Interior to convey approximately 7 acres of specified land (in two parcels) within the Vicksburg National Military Park to Mississippi for an interpretive center.
The conveyed land must facilitate public access to the park, may not be used in a manner that adversely impacts the park's resources or visitor experience, and remains subject to any use restriction that Interior determines is appropriate.
Interior must convey the land by quitclaim deed and without consideration, such as payment. Upon the conveyance of the land, Interior must modify the park's boundary to exclude the land.
posts.summaryLabel: Congressional Research Service, Reported to House
posts.meta: Natural Resources Committee · Rep. Bennie Thompson (D-MS)
posts.whatsNext: Takes effect (on enactment unless the text sets other dates)

aiSummaries.text:
The Vicksburg National Military Park Boundary Modification Act would require the Department of the Interior to transfer about 7 acres of land, in two separate parcels, within Vicksburg National Military Park to the State of Mississippi so that a interpretive center can be built there.

The land has to be used in a way that helps the public reach the park. It cannot be used in any way that harms the park's resources or the experience of visitors. Interior may also place any use restrictions it considers appropriate on the land.

The land must be transferred by quitclaim deed, and the state does not have to pay for it. Once the transfer is complete, Interior must change the park's boundary so that the land is no longer part of the park.

posts.title: To require the Secretary of Agriculture to convey the Pleasant Valley Ranger District Administrative Site to Gila County, Arizona.
posts.label: 📜✍️ Signed by Pres. Trump

This bill directs the Forest Service to convey specified property to Gila County, Arizona, upon the county's submission of a written request for such conveyance. The property, identified as the Gila County Area, consists of approximately 232.9 acres of National Forest System land located in the Tonto National Forest in Arizona.
The county must use the land for the purposes of serving and supporting veterans. If any land conveyed under this bill ceases to be used for such purpose, all right, title, and interest in and to the land shall revert to the United States, at the discretion of the Forest Service.
The conveyance must be made with a quitclaim deed and without consideration (value, such as payment, provided in exchange for the property).
The Forest Service must not be required to provide any covenant or warranty for the land and improvements conveyed to the county under such conveyance.
As a condition of the conveyance, the county must pay all the costs associated with the conveyance, including any (1) surveys, (2) environmental analysis or resource survey required under federal law, and (3) analysis required to comply with certain provisions of the National Historic Preservation Act.

aiSummaries.text:
This bill would require the Forest Service to transfer about 232.9 acres of National Forest System land in the Tonto National Forest in Arizona, known as the Gila County Area, to Gila County. The transfer would happen once the county submits a written request for it.

The county must use the land to serve and support veterans. If the county stops using it for that purpose, ownership of the land goes back to the United States, if the Forest Service chooses to take it back.

posts.title: Critical Infrastructure Manufacturing Feasibility Act
posts.label: 📜✍️ Signed by Pres. Trump
posts.summary:
Critical Infrastructure Manufacturing Feasibility Act
This bill requires the Department of Commerce to study and report on products that are in high demand across the critical infrastructure sectors. Critical infrastructure sectors are those whose assets, systems, and networks are vital to national security, the economy, public health or safety, or any combination of those matters.
The study must (1) identify the products in high demand across those sectors that are being imported due to manufacturing, material, or supply chain constraints; and (2) analyze the costs, benefits, and feasibility of manufacturing those products in the United States.
posts.summaryLabel: Congressional Research Service, Introduced in House
posts.committee: Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee, Energy and Commerce Committee
posts.meta: Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee, Energy and Commerce Committee · Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA)
posts.whatsNext: Takes effect (on enactment unless the text sets other dates)

aiSummaries.text:
This bill asks the Department of Commerce to study products that are in high demand across the sectors the country depends on most, such as national security, the economy, public health, and public safety. These are called critical infrastructure sectors.

The study has two parts. First, it must identify which in-demand products in those sectors are being brought in from other countries because of problems with manufacturing, materials, or supply chains. Second, it must look at what it would cost and gain, and how practical it would be, to make those products in the United States.

posts.title: Clergy Act
posts.label: 📜✍️ Signed by Pres. Trump
posts.summary:
Clergy Act
This act establishes a two-year window for members of the clergy who have opted out of Social Security and Medicare taxes (and are thus ineligible for benefits under those programs) to opt back in.
Under current law, certain ministers, members of religious orders, and Christian Science practitioners who object to participation in public insurance programs on religious or conscientious grounds may apply to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) for an exemption from Social Security and Medicare taxes on ministerial earnings. Individuals who are approved for the exemption do not receive Social Security or Medicare benefits in retirement unless they have qualifying credits from other employment. The exemption is irrevocable.
Under the act, clergy members may choose to revoke their exemption by filing an application with the IRS by the due date of their federal income tax return for the second taxable year after December 31, 2028 (i.e., April 15, 2031, unless an individual obtains an extension to file their taxes). A clergy member may choose for the revocation to take effect in taxable year 2029 or taxable year 2030. A revocation under the act is permanent.
Clergy members who opt back in will generally need 10 years of covered employment (40 credits) to be eligible for Social Security and Medicare benefits, as is currently required for these programs.
The IRS must develop a plan to inform clergy members of their eligibility to revoke prior exemptions, pursuant to the act's changes.
posts.summaryLabel: Congressional Research Service, Public Law
posts.committee: Finance Committee, Ways and Means Committee
posts.meta: Finance Committee, Ways and Means Committee · Rep. Vince Fong (R-CA)
posts.whatsNext: Takes effect (on enactment unless the text sets other dates)

aiSummaries.text:
This law gives clergy members who previously opted out of Social Security and Medicare taxes a two-year window to opt back in. Clergy who chose the exemption, which is normally permanent, could not receive those programs' retirement benefits unless they had qualifying work credits from other jobs.

Under current law, certain ministers, members of religious orders, and Christian Science practitioners who object to public insurance programs for religious or conscientious reasons can apply to the IRS to be exempt from Social Security and Medicare taxes on their ministry earnings. Those approved do not get Social Security or Medicare benefits in retirement unless they have qualifying credits from other work.

Under the new law, clergy members can revoke their exemption by filing an application with the IRS by the due date of their federal income tax return for the second tax year after December 31, 2028. That is April 15, 2031, unless they get an extension. They can choose for the change to take effect in 2029 or 2030, and once revoked, the decision is permanent.

Clergy who opt back in will generally need 10 years of covered work, or 40 credits, to qualify for Social Security and Medicare benefits, the same requirement that applies to these programs now.

The IRS must also create a plan to tell clergy members that they can now revoke their earlier exemptions.

posts.title: Romance Scam Prevention Act
posts.label: 📜✍️ Signed by Pres. Trump
posts.summary:
Romance Scam Prevention Act
This bill requires online dating service providers (i.e., mobile applications or websites) to provide users with a fraud ban notification if the user has established an account with the service and received a message through the service from a banned user of the service.
The fraud ban notification must include (1) the username or other profile identifier of the banned user and the most recent time when the user who is receiving the notification sent or received a message through the service to or from the banned user, (2) a statement that the banned user may have been using a false identity or attempting to defraud other users, (3) a statement that the user should not send cash (or another form of currency) or personal financial information to another user, (4) information about avoiding online fraud (e.g., a link to another website or a disclosure) and (5) contact information for the provider's customer service department.
The bill provides for enforcement of these requirements by the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general.
posts.summaryLabel: Congressional Research Service, Introduced in House
posts.meta: Energy and Commerce Committee · Rep. David Valadao (R-CA)
posts.whatsNext: Takes effect (on enactment unless the text sets other dates)

aiSummaries.text:
This bill, called the Romance Scam Prevention Act, requires online dating services, whether they run as phone apps or websites, to warn users about possible scammers. If a user has an account and has received a message through the service from someone who has since been banned, the service must send that user a fraud ban notification.

The notification must include the banned user's username or other profile identifier, and the most recent time the notified user sent or received a message to or from that person. It must also say that the banned user may have been using a fake identity or trying to defraud people. It must tell the user not to send cash, another form of currency, or personal financial information to anyone on the service. It must give information about avoiding online fraud, such as a link to another website or a disclosure. Finally, it must provide contact information for the service's customer service department.

The Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general would be responsible for enforcing these requirements.

posts.title: Retire through Ownership Act
posts.label: 📜✍️ Signed by Pres. Trump
posts.summary:
Retire through Ownership Act
This bill allows the fiduciary of an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) to rely on a valuation provided by an independent valuation expert or business appraiser in determining the fair market value of the plan's securities if the securities are not traded on a national securities exchange (i.e., not publicly traded) and the expert or appraiser follows specified methodologies.
In general, ESOPs are defined contribution pension plans where employees accrue shares of their employers' stock in individual accounts as part of their compensation. After separating from employment or retiring, employees receive the cash value of their shares.
Under the bill, an independent expert or appraiser must adhere to the methodology established under the Internal Revenue Service Ruling 59-60, which prescribes the factors a professional business appraiser should consider in forming a valuation of the stock for a closely held business.
posts.summaryLabel: Congressional Research Service, Passed Senate
posts.committee: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee
posts.meta: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee · Sen. Roger Marshall (R-KS)
posts.whatsNext: Takes effect (on enactment unless the text sets other dates)

aiSummaries.text:
The Retire through Ownership Act lets the trustee of an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) rely on a valuation from an independent valuation expert or business appraiser when setting the fair market value of plan stock that is not publicly traded. The expert or appraiser must follow the methods set out in the bill.

ESOPs are retirement plans in which employees earn shares of their employer's stock in individual accounts as part of their pay. When an employee leaves the job or retires, they receive the cash value of those shares.

Under the bill, the independent expert or appraiser must use the approach in Internal Revenue Service Ruling 59-60. That ruling lists the factors a professional business appraiser should consider when valuing stock in a closely held business.

Illegal Red Snapper and Tuna Enforcement Act
This act directs the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to jointly develop a standard methodology for identifying the country of origin of seafood to support enforcement against illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing (IUU fishing) and seafood fraud.
NOAA and NIST must consult with U.S. Customs and Border Protection and the Coast Guard in developing the methodology, which must use chemical analysis to identify the country of origin of seafood. The methodology must be consistent with the needs of federal and state law enforcement agencies in combating IUU fishing and seafood fraud. The methodology must also include a portable field kit and, to the extent practicable, be appropriate for testing prepared food (including raw preparations of seafood such as sushi). The agencies must conduct pilot studies of the methodology on red snapper and tuna.
Within two years after the act's enactment, NIST must report to Congress regarding the methodology and a plan for operationalizing it. The report must explain any aspects of its methodology that are impracticable, whether additional research would make the methodology practicable, and whether an alternate approach might be practicable.

Southcentral Foundation Land Transfer Act of 2025
This bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to convey approximately 3.4 acres in Anchorage, Alaska, to the Southcentral Foundation (SCF) for use in connection with health and social services programs.
The conveyance must be made by warranty deed. The conveyance may not (1) require any consideration (such as payment) from the SCF for the property; (2) impose any obligation, term, or condition on the SCF relating to that property; or (3) allow for any U.S. reversionary interest in the property.
HHS must be accorded any easement or access to the property as may be reasonably necessary to satisfy any retained obligation or liability of HHS.
The bill prohibits the SCF from being liable for certain environmental contamination that occurred on or before the date on which the property is conveyed to the SCF. In turn, HHS may not be liable for any contamination that occurred after the date that the SCF controlled, occupied, and used the property.

Critical infrastructure sectors are those whose assets, systems, and networks are vital to national security, the economy, public health or safety, or any combination of those matters.
The study must (1) identify the products in high demand across those sectors that are being imported due to manufacturing, material, or supply chain constraints; and (2) analyze the costs, benefits, and feasibility of manufacturing those products in the United States.

This bill asks the Department of Commerce to study products that are in high demand across the sectors the country depends on most, such as national security, the economy, public health, and public safety. These are called critical infrastructure sectors.

First, it must identify which in-demand products in those sectors are being brought in from other countries because of problems with manufacturing, materials, or supply chains. Second, it must look at what it would cost and gain, and how practical it would be, to make those products in the United States.

posts.title: Romance Scam Prevention Act
posts.label: 📌 Presented to President
posts.summary:
Romance Scam Prevention Act
This bill requires online dating service providers (i.e., mobile applications or websites) to provide users with a fraud ban notification if the user has established an account with the service and received a message through the service from a banned user of the service.
The fraud ban notification must include (1) the username or other profile identifier of the banned user and the most recent time when the user who is receiving the notification sent or received a message through the service to or from the banned user, (2) a statement that the banned user may have been using a false identity or attempting to defraud other users, (3) a statement that the user should not send cash (or another form of currency) or personal financial information to another user, (4) information about avoiding online fraud (e.g., a link to another website or a disclosure) and (5) contact information for the provider's customer service department.
The bill provides for enforcement of these requirements by the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general.

aiSummaries.text:
This bill, called the Romance Scam Prevention Act, requires online dating services, whether they run as phone apps or websites, to warn users about possible scammers. If a user has an account and has received a message through the service from someone who has since been banned, the service must send that user a fraud ban notification.

The notification must include the banned user's username or other profile identifier, and the most recent time the notified user sent or received a message to or from that person. It must also say that the banned user may have been using a fake identity or trying to defraud people. It must tell the user not to send cash, another form of currency, or personal financial information to anyone on the service. It must give information about avoiding online fraud, such as a link to another website or a disclosure. Finally, it must provide contact information for the service's customer service department.

The Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general would be responsible for enforcing these requirements.

posts.summary:
Cybersecurity for Small Businesses Act of 2026
This bill requires the Small Business Administration (SBA) to provide cybersecurity information and resources to small businesses, including resources for businesses seeking to contract with the federal government.
Specifically, the SBA must develop and distribute resources to assist small businesses in strengthening their cybersecurity infrastructure and implementing best practices.
Further, in coordination with the Department of Defense (DOD) and other appropriate federal agencies, the SBA must provide information and resources on the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) program to small businesses seeking to contract with the federal government. (CMMC is a cybersecurity framework for DOD contractors; certification is mandatory for contractors with access to certain controlled information.) The information and resources provided to small businesses must include certain existing DOD resources.
Finally, the SBA must report annually to Congress with information on small businesses that have contacted the SBA about cybersecurity.

aiSummaries.text:
The Cybersecurity for Small Businesses Act of 2026 directs the Small Business Administration (SBA) to give small businesses information and tools for protecting themselves against cyber threats. The SBA must create and share resources that help small businesses strengthen their cybersecurity systems and follow recommended good practices.

The bill also focuses on small businesses that want to sell goods or services to the federal government. The SBA must work with the Department of Defense (DOD) and other relevant federal agencies to share information about the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) program. CMMC is a cybersecurity framework for companies that work with the DOD, and certification is required for contractors that have access to certain controlled information. The materials given to small businesses must include some existing DOD resources.

Finally, each year the SBA must report to Congress on the small businesses that have contacted it about cybersecurity.

Specifically, the bill expands the public policy goals that allow a CDC to qualify for assistance to include additional objectives. These include (1) workforce development through work-based or work-integrated training, and (2) aiding the revitalization of an area for which a disaster has been declared or determined.
The bill also authorizes a CDC to take specified actions to facilitate the closing of 504 loans, such as correcting borrower or lender information on loan documents or reallocating up to 10% of the cost of a project.
Further, the bill allows small businesses to lease a larger portion of renovated buildings that are financed with 504 loans to other tenants in certain circumstances. In the case of a project to renovate or reconstruct an existing building, a small business may lease a maximum of 66% of the building to commercial or residential tenants if certain conditions are met. For example, the small business must have occupied the building for 12 consecutive months prior to the project.
Additionally, the bill exempts CDCs from the requirement to demonstrate they are unable to obtain credit elsewhere to receive 504 loans.

posts.title: Ratepayer Protection Act
posts.label: 🗳️ Motion to proceed filed
posts.summary:
Ratepayer Protection Act
The bill requires state utility regulators and nonregulated utilities to consider implementing a standard to hold certain large-load customers responsible for the costs associated with any generation, transmission, or distribution upgrade of electric service necessary to serve such customers. A large-load customer means a non-residential electric consumer that enters, or requests to enter, an agreement concerning the sale of electric energy primarily to operate information technology infrastructure and related systems pertaining to data storage and computational applications and services (e.g., data centers) that have a peak electric demand of 100 megawatts or more at a single site or campus.
Specifically, the bill requires states to consider implementing a federal standard for large-load customers. The standard must require rates charged by electric utilities for providing electric service to a large-load customer to be designed to recover from the large-load customer the full, incremental cost of any generation, transmission, or distribution upgrade necessary to serve such customer. This rate must include the costs that would be incurred if the large-load customer terminates an agreement with the electric utility pertaining to the sale of electric energy or otherwise ceases the purchase of energy from the electric utility.
Under the standard, an electric utility must require the large-load customer to provide to the utility financial assurances or contributions to cover the cost of any generation, transmission, or distribution upgrade that is necessary to serve the load of a large-load customer before the utility makes any generation, transmission, or distribution upgrade.
posts.summaryLabel: Congressional Research Service, Reported to House
posts.meta: Energy and Commerce Committee · Rep. Gabe Evans (R-CO)
posts.whatsNext: The Senate votes on taking it up (the motion can be withdrawn)

aiSummaries.text:
This bill asks state utility regulators and nonregulated utilities to consider a standard that makes large electricity users pay for the power system upgrades needed to serve them. The "large-load customers" it covers are non-residential customers, such as data centers, that buy electricity mainly to run computing and data storage operations and have a peak demand of 100 megawatts or more at a single site or campus.

Under the proposed standard, the rates a utility charges these customers would have to be set so that the customer covers the full added cost of any new power generation, transmission, or distribution upgrade needed to serve it. The rates would also have to cover the costs the utility would still face if the customer ends its agreement or stops buying power from that utility.

The standard would also require utilities to collect financial assurances or contributions from the large-load customer before they build any generation, transmission, or distribution upgrade needed to serve that customer.

posts.title: End Tax Penalties on American Hostages Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary:
End Tax Penalties on American Hostages Act
This bill extends certain federal tax deadlines for U.S. nationals who are unlawfully or wrongfully detained abroad or held hostage abroad and their spouses. The bill also allows for an abatement and refund of additional taxes, interest, and penalties assessed to such individuals for failing to meet a federal tax deadline during a period of detention.
Specifically, under the bill, the time period during which a U.S. national is unlawfully or wrongfully detained abroad or held hostage abroad is disregarded in determining certain federal tax deadlines, including deadlines for
filing a return for and paying federal income, estate, gift, employment, or excise taxes;
a tax credit or refund claim; and
the determination, assessment, and collection of additional taxes, interest, or penalties.
The bill requires the Department of State and the Department of Justice to annually provide the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) with lists to identify U.S. nationals who qualify for an extension.
The bill also requires the IRS to (1) abate and refund additional taxes, interest, and penalties assessed for any tax year ending during a period of detention for which an extension of a federal tax deadline is permitted; and (2) establish a program allowing U.S. nationals unlawfully or wrongfully detained abroad or taken hostage abroad (or their spouse or dependent) to claim a refund of additional taxes, interest, and penalties assessed for any tax year ending during a period of detention from 2021 to the bill’s enactment date.

posts.committee: Finance Committee, Ways and Means Committee
posts.meta: Finance Committee, Ways and Means Committee · Rep. Claudia Tenney (R-NY)
posts.whatsNext: Presidential review (±10 days)

aiSummaries.text:
This bill gives tax relief to U.S. citizens who are wrongfully detained or held hostage in another country, along with their spouses. While someone is held, that time is not counted when deadlines for federal tax matters are figured. These deadlines include those for filing and paying income, estate, gift, employment, and excise taxes, for claiming a tax credit or refund, and for the IRS to determine, assess, and collect additional taxes, interest, or penalties.

The State Department and the Justice Department would each year send the IRS lists of people who qualify for these extensions.

The bill also requires the IRS to cancel and refund any extra taxes, interest, and penalties charged for a tax year that ended while a person was detained, as long as the deadline extension applies. In addition, the IRS would set up a program that lets detained or hostage-held Americans, or their spouses or dependents, ask for refunds of such extra charges for tax years ending during a detention from 2021 until the bill becomes law.

This bill does not apply to individuals who are elderly or disabled, who continue to have a 30-day notification requirement for emergency services.

Currently in emergency cases, the patient, an individual on behalf of the patient, or the medical care provider must, within 72 hours after the beginning of treatment for the condition or after admission to a health care facility, notify a PRC authorizing official of the need for the emergency medical care. This bill instead allows the patient, other individual, or provider to notify PRC within 15 days of the treatment or admission.

posts.title: Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act
posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary:
Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act
This bill eases restrictions for ecosystem restoration projects in designated floodways that meet certain risk criteria.
Under current National Flood Insurance Program requirements, such projects are generally prohibited in a designated floodway if the project would increase the area’s base flood elevation.
The bill establishes conditions under which a community may permit an ecosystem restoration project within a designated floodway that would result in an increase in base flood elevations. Specifically, the project may be permitted if (1) a professional engineer determines that the cumulative effect of the increase will be not more than 1 foot; (2) no insurable structure or critical infrastructure is located in an impacted area; and (3) the community submits an analysis to the Federal Emergency Management Agency on the project’s effects after the project is complete.
An ecosystem restoration project is defined by the bill as a project that manipulates the physical, chemical, or biological characteristics of a site with a goal of recovering, reclaiming, or improving the functions of an aquatic resource or floodplain.

aiSummaries.text:
The Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act makes it easier to carry out ecosystem restoration projects in designated floodways that meet certain risk conditions. Right now, federal flood insurance rules generally ban such projects in a designated floodway if they would raise the area's base flood elevation, meaning the expected height of floodwaters during a major flood.

Under the bill, a community may allow a restoration project in a designated floodway even if it raises base flood elevations, but only if three conditions are met. First, a professional engineer must determine that the combined increase will be no more than 1 foot. Second, no insurable structure or critical infrastructure can be located in an affected area. Third, the community must submit an analysis to the Federal Emergency Management Agency on the project's effects after it is complete.

The bill defines an ecosystem restoration project as one that changes the physical, chemical, or biological features of a site in order to recover, reclaim, or improve the functions of a water-related resource or floodplain.

posts.meta: Judiciary Committee · Sen. Ted Cruz (R-TX)

posts.summary:
Safe Access to Cash Act of 2026
This bill establishes new federal criminal offenses for robberies involving automated teller machines (ATMs), including stand-alone ATMs.
Specifically, the bill prohibits the robbery or attempted robbery of a person who is using or servicing an ATM. A violation is punishable by a fine, a prison term of up to 20 years, or both.
The bill also makes it unlawful to (1) tamper with, damage, remove, or steal an ATM without authorization and remove money or property from the ATM with the intent to steal it; or (2) receive, possess, conceal, store, barter, sell, or dispose of any money or property stolen from the ATM. A violation is punishable by a fine, a prison term (e.g., up to 10 years if the value of the stolen money and property exceeds $1,000), or both.
These new prohibitions apply with respect to any ATM owned, operated, or sponsored by a bank, credit union, or savings and loan association, regardless of whether the ATM is located on the physical premises of or owned and operated by the institution.
Finally, the bill establishes enhanced penalties for ATM-related criminal offenses (or attempted offenses) that involve a forcible assault or use of a dangerous weapon (up to 25 years in prison), the forced accompaniment of another person (up to 30 years in prison), or the killing of another person (any years or life in prison).

aiSummaries.text:
This bill creates new federal crimes for robbing or stealing from automated teller machines (ATMs), including ATMs that stand alone rather than being inside a bank. It covers robbing or trying to rob someone who is using or servicing an ATM, which can bring a fine, up to 20 years in prison, or both.

It also makes it illegal to tamper with, damage, remove, or steal an ATM without permission, or to take money or property out of one intending to steal it. Anyone who receives, keeps, hides, stores, trades, sells, or gets rid of money or property stolen from an ATM can also be charged. These offenses can bring a fine, a prison term, or both. For example, the prison term can be up to 10 years if the stolen money and property are worth more than $1,000.

These rules apply to any ATM owned, run, or sponsored by a bank, credit union, or savings and loan association, whether or not the machine is on that institution's premises or run by the institution itself.

Finally, the bill sets tougher penalties for these crimes, or attempts at them, when they involve violence or a dangerous weapon, which can mean up to 25 years in prison. If the crime involves forcing another person to go along, the penalty can be up to 30 years. If the crime results in someone being killed, the penalty can be any number of years or life in prison.

posts.label: ✅🏛️ Passed Senate (unanimous consent)
posts.summary:
Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act
This bill requires the Department of Labor to provide training and education to its employees on how to effectively assist law enforcement in detecting human trafficking.
The bill directs Labor to determine which employees should receive the training and education based on their official duties. Further, it requires the training and education to include information that is appropriate for the employees' location or environment; that reflects current trends and best practices for the location or environment; and that is relevant to detecting human trafficking, identifying suspected victims, and referring potential cases to the Department of Justice and other appropriate authorities.

Criminal History Access Act of 2026
This bill authorizes a new type of entity—peace officer standards and training agencies—to access criminal history record information maintained by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. The term peace officer standards and training agency means an agency of a state, the District of Columbia, or a U.S. territory that is authorized to set standards for the hiring, training, ethical conduct, and retention of its law enforcement officers through certification, licensing, or other similar qualification processes.
